terms.definition: A stellar remnant of about two solar masses packed into a ball roughly 20 km across, made almost entirely of neutrons — the densest object that is still not a black hole.
terms.function: The final core left when a superheavy star explodes.

terms.definition: The resistance of tightly packed neutrons when quantum rules forbid them from sharing the same state — it is what holds the star up.
terms.whyItMatters: It spells the end of the white dwarf family of support: lightest cores make white dwarfs, heavier ones make this.

terms.definition: A rotating neutron star whose radio beams sweep past Earth at regular intervals, making it appear to flash like a lighthouse.
terms.function: A cosmic clock — because the star's rotation is so steady, pulsars keep time accurately.

terms.definition: The leftover debris cloud of a supernova explosion; the core remnant (neutron star) sits at its center.
terms.whereItIs: The expanding cloud around a newborn neutron star
terms.whyItMatters: It carries fresh heavy elements into the galaxy.

terms.definition: The rule that a spinning object spins faster when its mass moves inward — the reason a collapsing star core becomes a rapidly spinning neutron star.
terms.function: Explains pulsar spin rates from a single turn a day to dozens a second.
